findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / no ACL or public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no ACL specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, leaving it reliant on account defaults and potentially exposed to public access; combined with no encryption, sensitive reports could be exposed.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set for a bucket storing ledger/financial export data, meaning data at rest is unencrypted.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated with this bucket to prevent accidental public exposure of sensitive ledger data.
The bucket stores model artifacts but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined to restrict public access to this bucket.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so runbook documents (which may contain sensitive operational/security details) are stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined to prevent public exposure of operational runbooks.
Despite containing audit logs and using log-delivery-write ACL, there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource to prevent misconfiguration leading to public exposure.

The uploaded vendor roster object is placed into a bucket with no encryption configuration and no explicit server-side encryption specified on the object, risking exposure of potentially sensitive vendor data.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recovery, which combined with no versioning increases risk of irreversible data loss that could be leveraged in an attack or accidental destructive operation.
